t.WT101:
Nice to meet you my name is Gabriel Aguiar Salazar, Im 32 years old, 
I live in Gravataí - Rio Grande do Sul - Brazil, with my parents, nowadays
I work from home for a consulting software company like software quality assurance engineer, since the pandemic. In my current routine, I try to share in parts, work, studies, family/hobbies.
I hold a degree in Systems Analysis and Development and have been working in the IT field since 2014.I was strongly influenced by my father and brothers, all of whom work in IT.the only exception is my sister, who works as a physical education teacher at a private school.
My mother is a homemaker; she takes care of all of us.

My hobbies are practice jiu-jitsu, run and lift weights, read, study things in my area, enjoy time with my family and friends. These hobbies related a Physical education, I wont practicing these days because Im recovering from a injury in my left arm that happend in a jiu-jitsu championchip in city a three months ago, I passed for a surjury in 04/08 basically 2 months ago, now Im making some light exersices at home.
The doctor cleared me to start physical therapy, Im searching near my home, but this service is too expensive, around 200 reias per session. He recommended twenty sessions. My insurance plan covers all sessions, but there are few places that accept it. So far I have continued doing some exercises at home.

In my free time, I enjoy studying topics related to my field that will benefit my career. To unwind, I like watching YouTube videos related to travel and trading, spending weekend afternoons with friends, having a barbecue (a strong tradition here in the south of the country), and reading articles about technology in general and artificial intelligence. I’m not much into partying. For some time now, I’ve been dedicating my free time and energy to activities that add value and will yield future results. Currently, Im fully focused on improving my English proficiency and programming skills prioritizing my career so that I can apply for international positions in the near future. Combining my technical background with English fluency will create a well-rounded profile. Ultimately, I aim to work in an English-speaking environment on a daily basis, or at least gain experience doing so. That is actually why I am writing this text, it serves as a supplementary task to help me achieve that goal soon.

Once I have fully recovered from my surgery and completed my physical therapy sessions, I hope to soon return to my weightlifting routine and practice jiu-jitsu. In the meantime, I’ve been going for walks and occasionally running to clear my mind and relieve daily stress. I believe I’ll be back to my regular activities by the end of the year.
Typically, in cases like mine, it takes 4 to 6 months to recover and resume an active lifestyle.
Since it is a contact sport, I need to be extra careful and follow medical advice. At the 90-day mark post-surgery, I’ll have a follow-up appointment to get an update on my progress and current status. I hope this brief text has given you a chance to get to know me a little better.

t.WT102:
Saturday is one of my favorite days of the week, because it gives me time to focus on myself and on my personal development. Even though it’s the weekend, I like to wake up early, usually around 8:00 a.m. or even earlier. I’ve never been the kind of person who sleeps until noon, because I feel that the morning is the most productive part of my day. As soon as I get up, I take care of my personal hygiene and then have breakfast calmly, without rushing. During the week, mornings are usually busy, so on Saturdays I enjoy having my coffee slowly and starting the day in a peaceful way.

After breakfast, I like to study. I believe that continuous learning is essential in my career, especially in technology, where everything changes very quickly. That’s why I keep taking courses in my field. I usually use two platforms: Alura and Asimov Academy, and both are related to technology. Asimov’s courses are more focused on artificial intelligence and data, which are topics I find fascinating and increasingly important in the market. Alura, on the other hand, covers all areas of IT, so it helps me strengthen my knowledge in software quality, testing, programming, and other subjects that are useful in my daily work. Studying on Saturday mornings helps me stay up to date and gives me new ideas that I can apply in my projects.

I usually keep this study routine until noon, when I stop for lunch. Taking a break is important, because it helps me rest my mind and come back with more energy later. While I have lunch, I like to watch the lunchtime news to see what’s happening in the capital, Porto Alegre, and the surrounding region. I think it’s important to stay informed about local news, such as traffic, weather, events, and anything else that might affect my life or my community. Afterwards, I have a little coffee, as usual. For me, this coffee after lunch is almost a tradition, and I rarely skip it.

In the afternoon, my plans depend on how things are at home. If I don’t have any appointments or household chores to help with, I go back to studying for a few more hours. However, that doesn’t always happen, because there’s always something to do in the yard, like tidying up, cleaning, or organizing things. I don’t mind helping, though. Doing some physical work outside is a good way to take a break from the computer screen, and it feels good to see the house clean and organized.

In the late afternoon on Saturdays, I like to walk in the park near my house. It’s a pleasant place, and walking there helps me relax and clear my head after a full day. It’s also a good opportunity to get some fresh air and stay active, since I spend a lot of time sitting during the week. If I’m feeling motivated, I even go for a run. Running gives me a great sense of accomplishment and helps me release stress.

At the end of the day, I usually enjoy time with my family, which is one of the most important moments of my weekend. We often order some takeout, eat together, talk, and rest. After that, I like to look for some travel videos to watch, because I enjoy discovering new places and dreaming about future trips. Sometimes, instead of videos, we choose a movie to watch together. This is my way to switch off my mind for a while and recharge my energy for the next day.

t.WT104:
My Bedroom Office

The most important place of my day is my bedroom, because it is also my office. Since the pandemic, I have worked from home as a software quality assurance engineer, so I spend most of my day here, from Monday to Friday, usually more than eight hours.

My room has a comfortable size, about five square meters. There is my bed, a wardrobe, and a desk with a laptop, a second monitor, and a headset for daily meetings. I also keep my books on a shelf and my indoor bike in the corner, next to my dumbbells for physical therapy.

This room has many purposes: I work, study English, exercise, read, and sleep here. To separate work from rest, I organize my desk and log off at the same time every day.

t.LONG_VIDEO:
AI brain fry is real. Here's what leaders can do - Julie Bedard (TED@BCG)
https://www.ted.com/talks/julie_bedard_ai_brain_fry_is_real_here_s_what_leaders_can_do

Summary:
Workers are redesigning their jobs around AI and getting more done, but the people who oversee AI tools the most suffer from "AI brain fry." A BCG study of 1,488 U.S. workers links this mental fog to more fatigue, more mistakes and a higher intent to quit. To prevent it, leaders should protect people's attention, keep humans accountable for the AI's work, and shape this change instead of letting it happen to them.

Key sentences:
"Workers everywhere are quietly redesigning their jobs around AI."
"We need to shape this change rather than let it happen to us."

t.WT105:
My mother, Dona Estacelina, is the heart of our family. I live with my parents, and every day I see how much she dedicates herself to the house and to each of us. She is always attentive, worried about whether someone has eaten, slept well, or is facing a problem. This constant care is her most sincere way of showing love.

Throughout her whole life, my mother devoted herself to raising her four children. From an early age, she encouraged us to study and was also firm about it, because she knew that education would open doors for our future. Thanks to her and my father, today all of us have graduated. Every diploma we earned carries a little of her effort, her sacrifices, and her patience.

Recently, after much insistence, she finally started doing water aerobics (hidroginastica). At 60 years old, this activity is essential to prevent muscle loss, strengthen her body, and keep her energy up. It was a joy to see her take this step and think a little more about herself, after so many years of putting everyone else first. She comes back from her classes in a better mood, which makes us very happy.

Now, all that is left is to motivate my father to follow her example and exercise too. With my mother’s persistence, it will not take long.

I am deeply grateful for everything she has done and continues to do for us. My mother is an example of love, dedication, and strength, and she deserves all the care she has always given us.

t.WT106:
Today’s object of the day is my MIDI keyboard, because I bought a new cable to connect it to my computer. I had lost the old one, and I want to start studying keyboard again. This made me think about two keyboards: my Alesis with 49 keys and my brother’s Akai Mini with 25 keys.

A few days ago, I visited my brother, who also enjoys music production, and I tried his Akai Mini. It is far more compact than my Alesis, so it fits in a backpack. This makes it perfect for someone who wants to make music anywhere. However, with only 25 keys, it is not as versatile as a bigger keyboard. Depending on the song you want to study, two octaves are not enough.

My Alesis, on the other hand, is not as portable as the Akai, but it offers almost twice as many keys. While the Akai is great for beats and short melodies, the Alesis is far more useful for classical music than a small controller, because you need both hands and a wider range of notes. Whereas a small controller is ideal for quick ideas, a larger one is better for serious practice.

In the end, both objects are important, but for different reasons. The Akai Mini is the better choice for travel and convenience, while the Alesis 49 is the right tool for my goals. Since I want to study seriously and play classical pieces, my Alesis is the one I will use every day. Thanks to my new cable, it is ready to play again.
t.notes:
Tradução

O objeto do dia de hoje é o meu teclado MIDI, porque comprei um cabo novo para conectá-lo ao computador. Eu tinha perdido o antigo e quero voltar a estudar teclado. Isso me fez pensar em dois teclados: o meu Alesis, de 49 teclas, e o Akai Mini do meu irmão, de 25 teclas.

Há alguns dias, visitei meu irmão, que também gosta de produção musical, e experimentei o Akai Mini dele. Ele é muito mais compacto que o meu Alesis e cabe numa mochila. Por isso, é perfeito para quem quer fazer música em qualquer lugar. Porém, com apenas 25 teclas, ele não é tão versátil quanto um teclado maior. Dependendo da música que você quer estudar, duas oitavas não são suficientes.

O meu Alesis, por outro lado, não é tão portátil quanto o Akai, mas oferece quase o dobro de teclas. Enquanto o Akai é ótimo para batidas e melodias curtas, o Alesis é muito mais útil para música clássica, em que você precisa das duas mãos e de uma extensão maior de notas. Um controlador pequeno é ideal para ideias rápidas, ao passo que um maior é melhor para a prática séria.

No fim, os dois objetos são importantes, mas por motivos diferentes. O Akai Mini é a melhor escolha para viagens e praticidade, enquanto o Alesis 49 é a ferramenta certa para os meus objetivos. Como quero estudar a sério e tocar peças clássicas, o Alesis é o que vou usar todos os dias. Graças ao cabo novo, ele está pronto para tocar de novo.

t.SONG:
Kendrick Lamar - Alright
https://genius.com/6352012

Expressões

“Gon’ be alright”: forma falada de “gonna be alright”, ou “vai ficar tudo bem”. É o refrão e o grito de resistência da música. Ex.: Don’t worry, we gon’ be alright.
“(God) got us”: “to have got someone” = “estar do lado de alguém, cuidar de alguém”. Ex.: Relax, I got you (“Relaxa, tô contigo”).
“Been down before”: “to be down” aqui é “estar na pior, por baixo”. Sem o have (de we’ve been), o que é típico do AAVE. Ex.: We’ve been down before, we’ll get through this.
“All my life I has to fight”: referência ao filme/livro A Cor Púrpura. O “I has” é intencionalmente fora da gramática padrão (seria I’ve had to) e marca a voz e a origem.
“Forty acres and a mule”: referência histórica à promessa (nunca cumprida) de terra para ex-escravizados após a Guerra Civil americana. Usada como símbolo de reparação negada.

Gírias

Po-po: polícia. Ex.: Slow down, the po-po’s right there.
Lucy: apelido para Lucifer, o diabo. Kendrick o usa como personificação da tentação (fama, dinheiro).
Benjamins: notas de 100 dólares (que têm o rosto de Benjamin Franklin), ou seja, dinheiro. Ex.: It’s all about the Benjamins.
Homie: amigo próximo, parceiro, “mano”. Ex.: He’s my homie since high school.
F’d up (fucked up): tem dois sentidos. Pode ser “tô mal, destruído” (física ou emocionalmente) ou “você vacilou”. Ex.: I’m so f’d up after that week.

t.WT107:
Two Places, One Sunday

On Sunday, October 25th, I spent my day between two very different places, and both of them were special to me.

The first place was my own home. As usual here in the South of Brazil, Sunday is barbecue day. The whole family gets together at my parents’ house, where all the children meet to eat, talk, and laugh. The smell of the meat on the grill, the conversations around the table, and the relaxed atmosphere make home a place of comfort and rest. There, I can forget about work and simply enjoy time with the people I love.

The second place was the polling station, a school where I voted in the election for the new president of Brazil. Unlike my home, it was a place of duty and responsibility. People waited quietly in line, and the atmosphere was calm and serious. Even though I stayed there for only a few minutes, it was one of the most important moments of the day, because voting is how citizens help decide the future of the country.

Luckily, the school is only 500 meters from my house, so the whole trip was quick and easy. I walked there, voted, and twenty minutes later I was back home, just in time to join my family for lunch.

In the end, these two places showed me two sides of my life. Home reminded me of family, love, and tradition, while the polling station reminded me of my role as a citizen. Both are essential to who I am.
